search_log: Searched "Hello Beautiful" "Ann Napolitano" excerpt publisher; found the Penguin Random House title page and an authorized Penguin UK 40-page sample.
Searched "Hello Beautiful" "third person", "point of view", "narrator", and "multiple perspectives"; found explicit whole-book descriptions from GradeSaver and a completed-reader review.
Opened the publisher sample and inspected its sustained opening prose, including the transition from William's to Julia's focalization.
Opened the GradeSaver and A Viking in LA pages and verified that their statements referred to the novel's narration rather than synopsis grammar.

Searched BookRags and review sources for structural corroboration; BookRags confirmed rotating perspectives among William, Sylvie, Julia, and Alice but did not explicitly name grammatical person, so it was not treated as direct person support.

Ran exact-phrase context searches for q07956, q07959, and q07961; these resolved the apparent first-person material as a recited proverb and Emeline's dialogue, and restored William's omitted third-person thought frame.
Targeted searches of Kirkus and BookBrowse did not yield accessible explicit narration-person evidence; no credible source described sustained first- or second-person sections.
person_note: The controlling narration is close third person with rotating focalization among several characters, not an alternation of grammatical person. Goodreads excerpts repeatedly provide sustained third-person access to Sylvie, Julia, and other characters, and this agrees independently with the authorized opening sample and explicit whole-book descriptions. The apparent first-person exception in q07959 is Emeline's dialogue, while q07956 is a proverb characters recite; neither is a first-person narrative section. Some isolated or clipped quotes remain locally nondiagnostic, but there is no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base narration.
